title: Load a press die, then cycle it with the two-hand control
instruction: Put the red blank into the die in front of the orange ram, take both grippers out of the press, then push the two green buttons at the same time, one with each gripper, and hold them until the ram has closed on the blank. Then let go of the buttons.
context: Press operators load a die and then cycle the ram with a two-hand control that keeps both hands out of the point of operation (O*NET 51-4031.00; OSHA 1910.217). The robot must use both arms as the control demands, after its grippers are out of the die, and must not cycle an empty die.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). A grey benchtop horizontal press, 2.5 kg, fixed by its weight: base plate 29 x 38 x 1 cm (x 20-49, y -19 to 19). On the plate, an open-topped die runs along x at y 0: two dark rails 1 cm wide and 4 mm high, 4.6 cm apart (x 27.4-40), closed at the front by a dark anvil block 1.2 x 6.6 x 2.5 cm (x 26.2-27.4). The orange ram face (4 cm wide, 1 cm tall, 2 mm above the plate) rests at x 40 at the back of the die and slides forward along it out of a grey housing (x 44-49, 9 cm wide, 6 cm tall). A blank set in the die sits at x 30, 6 mm behind the anvil. Two green 4 x 4 cm palm buttons sit at x 24, y 15 and x 24, y -15 inside dark 12 mm collars, their tops 5 cm above the table (8 mm travel, 0.5 N per mm). A red aluminium blank, 4 x 4 x 1.4 cm, 60 g, lies flat on the table at x 14, y 12. The ram moves forward at 6 cm/s only while both buttons are held down at least 5 mm, if the second was pushed within 0.5 s of the first; a button held longer than that locks the control until both are released. Releasing either button sends the ram back.
scoring: From the press's state and a photo. The blank is seated when it lies flat in the die (on the plate within 3 mm, tilted under 5 degrees), its centre within 4 mm of the die's centreline and from against the anvil to 6 mm behind its marked place. 0 at once and for the rest of the trial if the press base moves 1 cm or turns 5 degrees, if the ram moves forward more than 1.5 cm with the blank not seated, or if any part of a gripper is in the die zone (from the anvil's back to the ram's rest face, 6.6 cm wide, up to 8 cm above the plate) while the ram is more than 1.5 cm forward. Otherwise: 1.0 if the ram has closed the seated blank against the anvil (within 3 mm) and is back (within 5 mm of rest), both buttons are released, the blank is still seated and both grippers are out of the die zone, unchanged for 1 s; 0.75 if the ram closed on the seated blank; 0.5 if it started forward (1.5 cm) with the blank seated; 0.25 if the blank was seated in the die; else 0.
reset_notes: Let the ram return to the back of the die, lift the blank out and lay it flat on its marked square on the table; release both buttons.
fidelity: Rigid bodies from boxes; the ram and buttons are prismatic joints with spring drives. The two-hand relay is simulated in the control loop at 20 Hz and drives the ram's position target forward at 6 cm/s while enabled. The ram presses with a soft spring (about 3 N past contact), so a real build can use a foam-faced ram with a force-limited drive. Gripper position comes from joint angles; the die zone is checked at the pad tips and two points up the gripper.
